title: Secure random generation and password storage

videos.script: The last lesson is about two secrets every server keeps: the random tokens it hands out, and the passwords it must never be able to read. {{random}} java dot util dot Random is a formula. Give it the same seed and it gives the same numbers, which is perfect for a game and useless for a secret. {{secure}} SecureRandom takes its numbers from the operating system. Thirty-two of its bytes make a token nobody can guess, in forty-three characters. {{store}} Then passwords. A fast hash lets an attacker check five million guesses a second. PBKDF2 with six hundred thousand iterations allows seven. {{verify}} And last, checking a login against what was stored, and raising the cost later without asking anybody to change their password.
